hypothesis: Question: the qualified dev results so far say that between-patient *level* signal in voice medians is at or below noise (constant row-median reference idea-baseline-0 = 8.379 row RMSE still beats standardized Ridge on rows 8.523 and HistGradientBoosting 10.465, and the patient-median between-patient ridge idea-3f71f3 only reached 8.398 with a ~0.4% LOPO gain at heavy shrinkage). Every attempt so far has tried to explain between-patient variance. This proposal attacks the other variance component instead: because the supplied scores are linear interpolations between clinician visits, each patient's label is nearly an affine function of test_time, so the *within-patient* slope may be a much cleaner, lower-variance estimand than the patient level. Since a patient's intercept is unknowable for unseen patients, the term is only usable if test_time can be centered per patient on the evaluation side; idea-3f71f3's reported check that unlabeled evaluation rows separate into 7 clean exact (age,sex) clusters (sizes 112-145) makes that transductive centering feasible (explicitly acknowledged as transductive use of unlabeled inputs, no evaluation labels). Contrasting pre-execution outcomes: (E1) drift is consistent in sign/size across the 28 training patients, the LOPO-shrunk pooled slope is clearly nonzero, and constant + lambda*b*(test_time - cluster mean test_time) beats the constant reference on dev row RMSE without degrading equal-patient MAE >3% (would be the first mechanism in this project that reduces *within*-patient residual variance); (E2) per-patient slopes are heterogeneous in sign because interpolation direction depends on each patient's visit pair, the LOPO grid selects lambda=0, and the method reduces exactly to the constant reference - a clean negative result that would tell the remaining rounds to stop spending on temporal structure; (E3) slopes are real in training but (age,sex) clustering fails to isolate evaluation patients (merged or tiny clusters), in which case the reported fallback flag and cluster sizes distinguish an operational grouping failure from a genuine absence of drift signal. Unverified beyond the measured history above; the LOPO grid (4 level estimators x 5 shrinkage values) plus the explicit fallback notes are what make E1/E2/E3 separable from a single dev number. The program deliberately uses no sklearn fitted attributes and no underscore-prefixed names, because the previous round (idea-8f51cd) was rejected as an invalid action for private/reflection attributes rather than for any scientific reason.
